svg.title: Four Checks Before Enforcement Spend
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-preflight-authority-and-recoverability; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Checks Before Enforcement Spend; subtitle: Proceed only on documented facts; route unresolved issues to the responsible specialist.; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: Read nodes in order. A supported answer advances to the next check; an unresolved or adverse answer follows the stated hold, referral, or decline path. These are jurisdiction-specific reviews, not universal procedural instructions.; caption: A valid judgment can still be uneconomic or temporarily unenforceable. Verify authority, lawful scope, bankruptcy constraints, and net reachable value before spending.; stages: label: Authority and judgment life; value: Proceed with verified enforcement rights; otherwise hold for counsel review; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Match creditor identity, assignment documents, judgment terms, payments, appeal status, and renewal deadlines. California CCP section 683.020 illustrates the ten-year enforcement limit absent applicable renewal or exception. Federal Rule 69 generally points execution to state procedure.; label: Licensing, debt purpose, and data; value: Proceed within authorized scope; otherwise suspend affected research or contact; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Check applicable state and local collection licensing even for commercial files. Apply the purpose-based debt definition in 15 U.S.C. section 1692a and Regulation F where covered. Document any consumer-report permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. section 1681b; judgment status alone does not supply one.; label: Bankruptcy and protected property; value: Proceed only with resolved stay exposure and an asset-specific exemption analysis; numeric value: 3.0; detail: Refresh bankruptcy screening before enforcement. A potentially applicable 11 U.S.C. section 362 stay stops affected action pending counsel's determination or court relief. Review discharge effects under section 524, bankruptcy exemptions under section 522, and applicable state execution exemptions.; label: Priority and incremental economics; value: Proceed on positive expected contribution; otherwise defer or decline spending; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Verify liens, perfection, timing, ownership, and likely sale or collection costs. State-enacted UCC section 9-317 may affect lien-creditor priority. An illustrative 40% chance of collecting $50,000 at a 25% fee produces $5,000 expected fees; subtracting $6,000 incremental operator costs produces a $1,000 expected loss.
